passages.text: And Job continued his discourse: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me, when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness, when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent, when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me, when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
passages.sermon:
Job spoke again.
Job was a righteous man who suffered greatly.
He said, “I wish I could return to earlier days.
I long for the months that are gone.
I remember the days when God watched over me.
God’s lamp shone above my head.
By God’s light, I walked through darkness.
I was in my prime.
God’s friendship rested on my tent.
The Almighty was with me.
My children were around me.
My steps were bathed in cream.
The rock poured out streams of oil for me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ מִֽי־ יִתְּנֵ֥נִי כְיַרְחֵי־ קֶ֑דֶם כִּ֝ימֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יִשְׁמְרֵֽנִי׃ בְּהִלּ֣וֹ נֵ֭רוֹ עֲלֵ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י לְ֝אוֹרוֹ אֵ֣לֶךְ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הָ֭יִיתִי בִּימֵ֣י חָרְפִּ֑י בְּס֥וֹד אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ עֲלֵ֣י אָהֳלִֽי׃ בְּע֣וֹד שַׁ֭דַּי עִמָּדִ֑י סְבִ֖יבוֹתַ֣י נְעָרָֽי׃ בִּרְחֹ֣ץ הֲלִיכַ֣י בְּחֵמָ֑ה וְצ֥וּר יָצ֥וּק עִ֝מָּדִ֗י פַּלְגֵי־ שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square, the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
passages.sermon:
Job was a respected man in his community.
He went out to the city gate.
He took his seat in the public square.
The young men saw Job.
The young men withdrew from him.
The old men saw Job.
The old men stood up when they saw him.
passages.original: בְּצֵ֣אתִי שַׁ֣עַר עֲלֵי־ קָ֑רֶת בָּ֝רְח֗וֹב אָכִ֥ין מוֹשָׁבִֽי׃ רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וִֽ֝ישִׁישִׁים קָ֣מוּ עָמָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his past honor.
Princes saw Job.
Princes stopped speaking.
Princes put their hands over their mouths.
passages.original: שָׂ֭רִים עָצְר֣וּ בְמִלִּ֑ים וְ֝כַ֗ף יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
passages.sermon:
The nobles sat in silence.
They did not speak.
Their voices became quiet.
Their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
They could not answer or respond.
passages.original: קוֹל־ נְגִידִ֥ים נֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם לְחִכָּ֥ם דָּבֵֽקָה׃

passages.text: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me, because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job was known for his righteousness and justice.
People who heard about Job called him blessed.
People who saw Job praised him.
Job rescued poor people who cried for help.
Job helped orphans who had no one to help them.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֹ֣זֶן שָׁ֭מְעָה וַֽתְּאַשְּׁרֵ֑נִי וְעַ֥יִן רָ֝אֲתָ֗ה וַתְּעִידֵֽנִי׃ כִּֽי־ אֲ֭מַלֵּט עָנִ֣י מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝יָת֗וֹם וְֽלֹא־ עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
passages.sermon:
I helped a dying man.
He blessed me.
I brought joy to a widow.
Her heart rejoiced because of me.
passages.original: בִּרְכַּ֣ת אֹ֭בֵד עָלַ֣י תָּבֹ֑א וְלֵ֖ב אַלְמָנָ֣ה אַרְנִֽן׃

passages.text: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job was known for his upright character.
Job says, “I put on righteousness.”
Righteousness covered me.
Justice was like my robe.
Justice was like my turban.
passages.original: צֶ֣דֶק לָ֭בַשְׁתִּי וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֑נִי כִּֽמְעִ֥יל וְ֝צָנִ֗יף מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃

passages.text: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
passages.sermon:
I helped people who could not see.
I guided the blind.
I helped people who could not walk.
I supported the lame.
passages.original: עֵינַ֣יִם הָ֭יִיתִי לַֽעִוֵּ֑ר וְרַגְלַ֖יִם לַפִּסֵּ֣חַ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job describes his actions.
Job cared for the needy.
He acted like a father to them.
Job helped people who had no one to defend them.
He investigated the case of the stranger.
He made sure justice was done for those who needed help.
passages.original: אָ֣ב אָ֭נֹכִֽי לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים וְרִ֖ב לֹא־ יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶחְקְרֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job describes his actions.
Job fought against unjust people.
Job broke the power of the wicked.
He shattered their fangs.
He rescued victims from their mouths.
He snatched the prey from their teeth.
passages.original: וָֽ֭אֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּע֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וּ֝מִשִּׁנָּ֗יו אַשְׁלִ֥יךְ טָֽרֶף׃

passages.text: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job cares for the needy and defends strangers.
Job says, “I thought I would die in my own home.”
He says, “I believed I would live a long life.”
He says, “I expected my days to be as many as the grains of sand.”
passages.original: וָ֭אֹמַר עִם־ קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע וְ֝כַח֗וֹל אַרְבֶּ֥ה יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a righteous man.
Job describes his life and blessings.

My roots spread out toward the water.
Dew rests on my branches each night.
passages.original: שָׁרְשִׁ֣י פָת֣וּחַ אֱלֵי־ מָ֑יִם וְ֝טַ֗ל יָלִ֥ין בִּקְצִירִֽי׃

passages.text: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking about himself.
\r\nHe says his glory is always new within him.
\r\nHe says his strength is renewed in his hand, like a bow made new.
\r\nHe feels refreshed and strong inside.
\r\nHe feels ready and able, as if holding a new weapon.
passages.original: כְּ֭בוֹדִי חָדָ֣שׁ עִמָּדִ֑י וְ֝קַשְׁתִּ֗י בְּיָדִ֥י תַחֲלִֽיף׃

passages.text: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
passages.sermon:
Men listened to me.
They expected something from me.
They waited quietly for my advice.
They did not speak while they waited.
They wanted to hear my counsel.
passages.original: לִֽי־ שָׁמְע֥וּ וְיִחֵ֑לּוּ וְ֝יִדְּמ֗וּ לְמ֣וֹ עֲצָתִֽי׃

passages.text: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
passages.sermon:
Job was a respected leader in his community.
People listened carefully when Job spoke.
After Job finished speaking, no one argued or replied.
Job’s words rested gently on the people.
His speech refreshed them like dew on the ground.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֣י דְ֭בָרִי לֹ֣א יִשְׁנ֑וּ וְ֝עָלֵ֗ימוֹ תִּטֹּ֥ף מִלָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
passages.sermon:
People waited for me.
They waited for me like people wait for rain.
They opened their mouths for my words.
They received my words like spring showers.
passages.original: וְיִֽחֲל֣וּ כַמָּטָ֣ר לִ֑י וּ֝פִיהֶ֗ם פָּעֲר֥וּ לְמַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
passages.sermon:
Job was a respected leader.
\r\nWhen I smiled at the people, they did not believe it.
\r\nMy smile surprised them.
\r\nThe light of my face was valuable to them.
\r\nThey treasured my approval.
passages.original: אֶשְׂחַ֣ק אֲ֭לֵהֶם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ינוּ וְא֥וֹר פָּ֝נַ֗י לֹ֣א יַפִּילֽוּן׃

passages.text: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job was once a leader among his people.
I chose the path for the people.
I sat as their chief.
I lived among them like a king among his soldiers.
I comforted those who mourned.
passages.original: אֶֽבֲחַ֣ר דַּרְכָּם֮ וְאֵשֵׁ֪ב רֹ֥אשׁ וְ֭אֶשְׁכּוֹן כְּמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּגְּד֑וּד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲבֵלִ֣ים יְנַחֵֽם׃
